headline.text: Concurrent acitretin and alcohol associated with formation of longer-lasting etretinate

reported.text: The label states concurrent acitretin and ethanol was associated with formation of etretinate with longer half-life.

mechanism.text: Concurrent ingestion of acitretin and ethanol has been associated with formation of etretinate with longer elimination half-life.

gaps.text: No confirming or contradicting human studies on alcohol-related etretinate formation found in these searches.
searched: etretinate formation acitretin alcohol ingestion trial

pharmacistQuestions.text: The label describes this interaction, but there seem to be no human studies of it. How is it usually handled for someone like me?
Do any of my other medicines or products, like cough syrup or mouthwash, contain alcohol?
Does my dose, or the time between taking acitretin and drinking alcohol, change how much this matters?

claims.text: The label states concurrent acitretin and ethanol was associated with formation of etretinate with longer half-life.
claims.quote: Clinical evidence has shown that concurrent ingestion of acitretin and ethanol has been associated with the formation of etretinate, which has a significantly longer elimination half-life than acitretin.
claims.judgeRationale: The quote explicitly states that concurrent acitretin and ethanol ingestion was associated with formation of etretinate with a significantly longer elimination half-life, supporting the stated mechanism.

claims.text: In crossover trial all 10 subjects formed etretinate taking single 100-mg acitretin with ethanol over 3 hours.
claims.quote: In a 2-way crossover trial, all 10 subjects formed etretinate with concurrent ingestion of a single 100-mg oral dose of acitretin during a 3-hour period of ethanol ingestion (total ethanol, approximately 1.4 g per kg body weight).
claims.judgeRationale: The quote directly reports that all 10 subjects in the 2-way crossover trial formed etretinate after a single 100-mg acitretin dose during 3 hours of ethanol ingestion, supporting the bounded mechanistic claim.

claims.text: The label lists increased alcohol intake among those with increased tendency to hypertriglyceridemia on acitretin.
claims.quote: Subjects with an increased tendency to develop hypertriglyceridemia included those with disturbances of lipid metabolism, diabetes mellitus, obesity, increased alcohol intake, or a familial history of these conditions.
claims.judgeRationale: The quote only lists increased alcohol intake as a predisposing characteristic for hypertriglyceridemia during acitretin therapy and does not report that the acitretin-alcohol combination increases risk or impose a restriction on that combination, so the increases_risk stance is unsupported.
